Subject: Review: Murmur Dialogue (Godot 4) — 4 stars, but read the 3.2 note first

---

4 stars. The tool earned more than that from me, but buying it today means buying it without support and with a broken latest version, and you should know that before you click buy.

I've used Murmur since v1.3 in 2022 and it's the reason Lanternfolk exists at all. The first prototype was literally a ferryman scene, built over one weekend with Murmur handling the branching. That scene is the reason I quit my job at a mobile studio and started making my own games. We're three weeks from launching Lanternfolk on Steam — 412 dialogue nodes, nine languages, every one of them exported through Murmur's CSV pipeline — and I owe this tool an honest review.

So, honestly:

What's broken in 3.2.0

3.2.0 has a save bug. Every Murmur variable comes back at its default value when you load a save made in 3.1.x. In our game that meant the ferryman forgot you'd already paid him, so the entire exchange falls apart. Nothing is corrupted on disk and your dialogue data is fine — the variables simply aren't being restored. If you were relying on a variable to track state across a conversation, this one will hurt.

The fix: roll back to 3.1.4

If you're on 3.2, downgrade. Take the 3.1.4 release and replace the Murmur folder in your project's addons folder with it. Keep a copy of 3.1.4 somewhere outside the project so an editor or a project manager doesn't quietly update you back to 3.2. Old saves load correctly under 3.1.4. I posted this on the forum in October and it turned into a thread of people confirming the same thing, so thanks to the person who added the "can confirm, 3.1.4 works" reply — that saved a lot of us the week.

That's the whole workaround, and it's reliable. If you're starting a brand new project with no 3.1.x saves, 3.2 is probably fine for you, but I wouldn't trust it with a shipped game until it's sorted.

The support situation

Ines has stepped back from Murmur. Her pinned update says 3.2 will be the last version and that she isn't reading the reviews or the forum any more, so don't expect a patch or a reply to a bug report. That, plus the 3.2 bug, is exactly why this is 4 stars instead of 5. The tool deserved better, but you're paying for it today either way.

On the review that says she took the money and ran

That one has been bothering me. I bought v1.3 for $19 in August 2022, and Ines gave us four years of updates after that — conditions, variables, barks, voice line hooks, and a CSV localisation export we still use every single day. Twenty-nine dollars is what it costs now; the early price was lower. She didn't take anyone's money and vanish. She shipped a version, then stepped back and said so plainly instead of quietly disappearing, and she left the source on a public repo under MIT instead of letting it rot behind a login. That's the opposite of running.

Someone will fork it, by the way. The source is MIT, so it's allowed, and I'd rather it be someone who's actually shipped a game with it. I've got Lanternfolk to launch first, but I'll be looking at the fork question properly in the new year. If you're a studio that got burned by 3.2 and need to keep your project alive, forking is a genuinely reasonable option — and I'd rather see that than a plugin dying in a listing.

Thanks

I don't know how else to put this, so I'll just put it: thank you, Ines. Four years of updates, a CSV export that got Lanternfolk into nine languages, and for leaving the source open and the door unlocked for whoever picks this up next. I hope you get some rest.

Still deciding? Buy it, but pin it at 3.1.4.

reasons: The piece says Ines 'isn't reading the reviews or the forum any more' and attributes it to her pinned update, but that comes from her private DM ('I can't read the reviews'), so it leaks private information.
